ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Immerse two inert electrodes in a nickel(II) fluoride $\ce{NiF2}$ solution, and pass a constant current of $2.20~\mathrm{A}$ through the circuit. Given the standard reduction potential list, how long does it take (in seconds) to deposit $1.2~\mathrm{g}$ of nickel on the cathode?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a standard reduction potential table, with the headers Half-reaction and E°. The table lists O2(g)+4H+ +4e−→H2O(l), E°=1.23 V; F2(g)+2e−→2F−, E°=2.87 V; 2H2O(l)+2e−→H2(g)+2OH−, E°=−0.83 V; Ni2+ +2e−→Ni(s), E°=−0.25 V. Reasoning: In the nickel(II) fluoride solution, reduction occurs at the cathode; from the potential table in the image, it can be confirmed that the cathode reaction in which nickel ions are reduced to nickel is Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s), that is, depositing 1 mol Ni requires 2 mol electrons. The problem gives the current I=2.20 A, and the target nickel mass m=1.2 g. The amount of substance of nickel n(Ni)=1.2/58.69≈0.02045 mol. The required amount of substance of electrons n(e−)=2×0.02045≈0.04089 mol. The required charge Q=nF≈0.04089×96485≈3.95×10^3 C. Time t=Q/I≈3947/2.20≈1.79×10^3 s. Therefore the required time is approximately 1790 s.
